Administer D365 licensing Base, Attach, Operations/Activity, and Team Member —right-sizing assignments to actual role requirements and identifying cost-reduction opportunities. Reconcile license consumption reports against assigned security roles and flag discrepancies, unused licenses, and users no longer with the organization. Maintain accurate documentation of roles, license mappings, and access-approval workflows; support renewal planning and true-up cycles with IT leadership and Microsoft partners. Bills of Materials (BOM) and Routing Administer BOM and formula structures, including creation, versioning, approval, activation, and expiration of BOM and route versions. Maintain routes, operations, resources, and resource groups in coordination with Manufacturing Engineering and Production. Enforce engineering change control: validate that BOM and routing changes are requested, reviewed, approved, and released through the documented change management process. Govern released product master data — item numbers, product dimensions, units of measure, costing, and item groups — that drives BOM accuracy. Support BOM calculation and standard cost roll-ups with Cost Accounting; troubleshoot variances traceable to structure or routing errors. Execute mass BOM updates, data imports, and cleanup projects using the Data Management framework, with validation and standardization plans. Provide BOM-based reporting to Engineering, Customer Experience, and Production so downstream teams can retrieve accurate as-built configurations. Product Configurator Own the D365 F&O product configuration models: constraint-based configuration, attributes, components, expression constraints, calculations, and user-requirement templates. Build and maintain configuration rules so quoting and order entry produce valid, manufacturable, correctly priced configurations. Maintain configurator-driven BOM and route logic so that generated structures match engineering intent and part-numbering standards. Test and validate model changes in sandbox environments prior to production release; maintain regression test cases for high-volume product families. Administer configurator security so that model authoring is restricted to authorized users while sales and customer service retain appropriate run-time access. Troubleshoot configurator errors, failed configurations, and pricing anomalies raised by Sales, Customer Service, and Production; coordinate vendor/partner escalation when required. Platform Administration and Support Serve as tier-2/tier-3 escalation for D365 F&O incidents; track root cause and drive permanent corrective action. Maintain standard operating procedures, configuration documentation, and end-user training materials. Participate in business continuity and disaster recovery planning for the ERP system. Qualifications Required Hands-on Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (or Dynamics AX 2012) administration experience. Demonstrated experience designing and maintaining D365 F&O security roles, duties, and privileges, including segregation of duties analysis. Working knowledge of D365 licensing models and license-to-role mapping. Practical experience with manufacturing master data: BOMs, formulas, routes, resources, and released products. Experience with the D365 product configurator (constraint-based configuration models). Proficiency with the Data Management framework for imports, exports, and configuration packages. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with clear written and verbal communication across technical and non-technical audiences. Preferred Experience in a regulated manufacturing environment Exposure to X++, OData/Data Entities, Power BI, or Power Platform. Performance Measures Completion of scheduled access reviews with documented business-owner approval. Reduction in segregation-of-duties conflicts and over-provisioned accounts. Accuracy of license assignments relative to role requirements and realized licensing savings. BOM and routing data accuracy, measured by production and costing exception rates. Configurator defect rate and time to resolve configuration-related order issues.

Follow up consistently with parents until outstanding payments are received or the matter is escalated to management. Maintain a clear record of all communication with parents, including call outcomes, payment promises, expected payment dates, and agreed arrangements. Monitor changes in children's attendance, room allocation, funding eligibility, and fee arrangements where these affect invoices, in coordination with the nursery management team. Ensure that payments, adjustments, credits, and funding-related changes are accurately reflected in the accounts. Escalate persistent non-payment, disputed invoices, or unresolved account discrepancies to management in a timely manner. 
 2. Learner Fee Management – Radiant Minds Education 
 Maintain complete and accurate fee records for learners enrolled in the organisation's training courses and qualification programmes. Track course fees, registration charges, instalment plans, payment deadlines, outstanding balances, and any agreed payment arrangements. Ensure that every learner has a clear payment record and that no instalment or scheduled payment is overlooked. Monitor upcoming instalment dates and contact learners in advance to remind them of their payment obligations. Make regular follow-up calls and send appropriate reminders to learners whose payments are due or overdue. Follow up on missed instalments, partial payments, failed transactions, and outstanding course fees until the matter is resolved or escalated. Maintain clear records of learner payment commitments, follow-up dates, responses, and reasons for delayed payments. Coordinate with admissions, course administration, assessors, and management where learner enrolment details or course changes affect payment arrangements. Identify learners with recurring payment delays and provide timely updates to management. Ensure all learner accounts remain accurate, transparent, and up to date throughout the duration of their enrolment. 
 3. Invoicing, Payment Tracking and Reconciliation 
 Raise and issue invoices accurately and within the required timelines. Maintain a centralised record of invoices raised, payments received, outstanding balances, and overdue accounts for both organisations. Verify payment information against available bank statements, payment confirmations, or authorised payment records. Record and allocate payments to the correct parent, child, learner, invoice, and payment period. Identify discrepancies between invoices, payments received, and outstanding balances. Investigate missing payments, duplicate entries, incorrect allocations, and differences in account balances. Maintain a clear audit trail of invoices, payment records, adjustments, and follow-up actions. Prepare regular reports showing total invoiced amounts, collections received, outstanding fees, overdue accounts, and upcoming payment deadlines. Support month-end account reviews and provide management with accurate collection and outstanding-payment summaries. Ensure that no invoice, payment, instalment, or overdue account is left unrecorded or without an appropriate follow-up action. 
 4. CRM and Financial Record Management 
 Maintain accurate and current records in the organisation's CRM, accounting software, spreadsheets, and other approved systems. Update each child's and learner's account with invoices, payments, outstanding balances, follow-up notes, and next action dates. Record every relevant phone call, email, reminder, payment commitment, and escalation in the CRM system. Ensure that the status of each account is clearly visible, such as paid, partially paid, due, overdue, awaiting confirmation, disputed, or escalated. Maintain a reliable follow-up schedule so that upcoming instalments and overdue accounts are never missed. Regularly review CRM records to identify missing information, overdue follow-ups, duplicate entries, and inconsistencies. Ensure that all financial records are organised, accessible to authorised staff, and maintained in accordance with internal procedures and data protection requirements. 
 5. Fee Collection and Follow-Up 
 Take full ownership of the fee collection process from invoice issuance through payment receipt and account closure. Make regular outbound calls to parents and learners regarding upcoming payments, overdue fees, and missed instalments. Follow a structured reminder process, including advance reminders, payment-due notifications, overdue follow-ups, and escalation where required. Communicate payment expectations, deadlines, outstanding balances, and approved payment arrangements clearly and professionally. Obtain realistic payment commitments from parents and learners and follow up on the agreed dates. Maintain a daily list of payments due, payments expected, overdue accounts, and pending follow-up actions. Prioritise high-value outstanding balances, long-overdue accounts, and accounts with repeated missed commitments. Ensure that no account remains unattended simply because a reminder was missed or a follow-up was not recorded. Escalate accounts that remain unpaid after the prescribed follow-up process, following management-approved procedures. Maintain a professional, respectful, and solution-focused approach while ensuring that payment obligations are communicated firmly and consistently. 
 6. Reporting and Management Updates 
 Prepare daily updates on payments received, payments expected, overdue accounts, and follow-up activities. Provide weekly collection reports separately for Rise ’N’ Shine Nursery and Radiant Minds Education. Maintain an updated list of all outstanding accounts, including the amount due, due date, duration overdue, last contact date, and next action. Highlight accounts where payment has been promised but not received. Report recurring collection issues, unusual payment patterns, and potential risks to cash flow. Support management with monthly summaries of total fees invoiced, total collections, outstanding balances, and collection performance. Ensure reports are accurate, timely, and supported by the underlying financial records. Proactively notify management of discrepancies, system issues, or any matter that could affect fee collection or financial accuracy. 
 Essential Skills and Requirements 
 Previous experience in accounts, billing, fee collection, credit control, accounts receivable, or payment follow-up. Strong numerical and analytical skills, with excellent attention to detail. Experience preparing invoices, tracking payments, managing outstanding balances, and maintaining financial records. Confidence in making regular outbound calls to parents, learners, customers, or clients regarding payments. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple accounts, payment deadlines, and follow-up schedules simultaneously. Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including maintaining trackers and preparing reports. Experience using CRM systems, accounting software, or other financial record-management tools. Ability to identify discrepancies, investigate payment issues, and maintain accurate records. Strong follow-through, accountability, and a proactive approach to resolving outstanding payments. Ability to work independently in a fully remote environment and manage time effectively. Professional handling of confidential financial and personal information. 
 Preferred Qualifications and Experience A degree, diploma, or relevant qualification in Accounting, Finance, Commerce, or Business Administration. Experience in accounts receivable, credit control, collections, or fee administration. Previous experience working with a nursery, childcare setting, education provider, training institute, or course-fee payment system. Experience maintaining CRM systems and preparing daily, weekly, and monthly financial reports. 
 Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Performance will be assessed against the following measures: 
 Invoice accuracy: Invoices are raised correctly and issued within the agreed timelines. Payment tracking: All payments received are recorded and allocated accurately. Collection follow-up: Every due and overdue account receives the required follow-up within the agreed timeframe. No missed instalments: All scheduled payments are tracked, with reminders and follow-ups completed as required. CRM accuracy: Account records, call notes, payment commitments, and next action dates are maintained consistently. Outstanding account management: Overdue balances are actively monitored, followed up, and escalated where necessary. Reporting: Daily, weekly, and monthly reports are submitted accurately and on time. Reconciliation: Payment discrepancies are identified and resolved or escalated promptly. Accountability: Promised payments and pending actions are monitored until resolved. Professional communication: Parents and learners receive clear, timely, respectful, and consistent payment communications. 
 Confidentiality and Professional Conduct 
 The Accounts Executive will have access to sensitive financial records, parent and learner contact details, and internal business information. The successful candidate must maintain strict confidentiality, follow approved data protection and information-security procedures, and use financial information only for authorised business purposes. 
 The candidate must not make unauthorised changes to fee structures, payment terms, refunds, discounts, or account adjustments. Any disputed payment, exceptional arrangement, or suspected discrepancy must be documented and referred to the appropriate manager. 
 What We Are Looking For We are looking for someone who takes ownership of their responsibilities and understands that accurate fee management is essential to the smooth running of both organisations.

They will actively monitor every account, anticipate upcoming payments, follow up on missed instalments, maintain accurate CRM records, and ensure that management always has a clear picture of the financial position. 
 The primary objective of this role is to ensure that every fee due is accounted for, every payment received is recorded, every outstanding balance is followed up, and no payment is missed due to a lack of tracking or follow-through.

title: Senior Financial Analyst
description:
Senior Financial Analyst 
 DigiAlly | Job Description | 19 October 2026 
 DigiAlly is seeking two Senior Financial Analysts with hands-on experience analysing companies. The role covers end-to-end company analysis on Indian companies, listed and unlisted - financial statements, ratios, business performance, peer comparison and financial health - together with research on the industries they operate in. 
 The position is full-time employment, fully remote, and suited to a CA and/or CFA with 5-7 years of relevant experience. 
 Role at a Glance 
 Title: Senior Financial Analyst Vacancies: 2 Location: Fully remote, India-based Employment Type: Full-time, permanent Experience: 5-7 years of hands-on company and industry analysis: financial statements, ratios and research on listed or unlisted companies Qualifications: CA (ICAI) and CFA charter preferred; candidates with one of the two, or an MBA (Finance) with an engineering degree, will be considered given strong relevant experience Reports To: Founder, DigiAlly Start Date: Immediate; no later than 15 days from offer 
 About DigiAlly 
 DigiAlly is a financial intelligence and credit risk firm headquartered in Thane, Maharashtra. We produce institutional-grade company analysis, credit assessments, peer benchmarking and investment research on Indian companies, listed and unlisted, across a wide range of industries. Our clients rely on this work to make lending, investment and partnership decisions. We hold our research to one standard: every figure traces to a primary source or a named database, and data gaps are disclosed rather than estimated. 
 The Role 
 The Senior Financial Analyst owns company and industry analysis end to end: researching the industry, sourcing filings, spreading financial statements, analysing ratios and business performance, assessing financial health and credit quality, writing the report, verifying it against primary sources and presenting it to clients. The role reports directly to the founder and carries full accountability for the accuracy of every deliverable. 
 Success in the role rests on five attributes: 
 Accuracy - Our reports inform lending and investment decisions. A misread audit opinion or a benchmark computed from a single peer rather than the full set is a material error, and detecting such errors before release is central to the role. Logical reasoning and problem solving - Framing an unfamiliar company or an incomplete set of filings as a clear analytical question, and working it through to a well-supported answer. Judgement - Converting ratios, filings and alternative data into a defensible view of a company's performance and financial health, with the strength of evidence behind each finding made explicit. Writing - Neutral, precise, well-structured prose in which metric comparisons replace adjectives. Independence - Managing several assignments in parallel, remotely, with full ownership of scope, versions and deadlines. 
 Key Responsibilities 
 Company Analysis: Analyse each company's business model, revenue and product mix, cost structure, capital allocation and growth drivers, and relate the financial trends to what the business is actually doing. Industry Research: Research the industry each company operates in - structure, size and growth, demand drivers, regulation, competitive dynamics and key players - and place the company's performance in that context. Financial Statement and Ratio Analysis: Spread standalone and consolidated financial statements from statutory filings, annual reports and financial databases. Compute and interpret the full ratio set - profitability, liquidity, leverage, efficiency, coverage and cash-flow ratios - alongside working-capital cycles, lease-adjusted leverage and restricted versus unrestricted cash. Prepare cash flow statements from the balance sheet and P&L where filings omit them. Financial Health and Credit Assessment: Produce structured assessments that evaluate financial health, earnings quality and payment behaviour, assign a risk category and document the rationale. Research Reports: Write full-length research reports on listed and unlisted companies covering industry context, business model, financial performance, capital raises, corporate milestones, governance and outlook. Peer Benchmarking: Construct peer sets, compute benchmark statistics across the full set and produce benchmarking presentations with supporting workbooks. Quality Assurance: Verify reports and presentations against source data before release, document discrepancies and tag each finding by evidence strength (primary filing, secondary database or unverified claim). Audit and Governance Review: Read audit reports precisely, distinguishing the opinion on financial statements from the opinion on internal financial controls. Track qualifications, emphasis-of-matter paragraphs, related-party transactions and registered charges. Alternative Data: Use statutory, tax and banking records as post-year-end and compliance signals beyond audited financials. Client Engagement: Prepare briefs for management and stakeholder interviews, present findings to clients and respond to follow-up queries. Methodology: Maintain analytical models, templates and review checklists, and propose improvements as new risk patterns emerge. 
 Qualifications and Experience 
 Professional Qualifications:- 
 Chartered Accountant (ICAI) - Preferred CFA Charterholder - Preferred MBA (Finance) - Acceptable, including for candidates with an engineering undergraduate degree 
 The ideal candidate holds both CA and CFA. Candidates with one of the two, or with an MBA (Finance), supported by directly relevant experience, are encouraged to apply. 
 Experience 
 5-7 years of hands-on experience analysing companies and their industries: reading financial statements, computing and interpreting ratios, and forming a view on business performance and financial health. Direct analytical experience is essential. Hands-on experience with Indian company financials under Ind AS and Indian GAAP, Companies Act filings and the MCA portal. A record of authored company analyses or research reports; writing samples will be requested. 
 Skills and Competencies 
 Technical Skills:- Fluent reading of balance sheets and P&L statements, including notes and schedules, and the ability to prepare a cash flow statement from them that reconciles to the movement in cash. Thorough knowledge of financial ratios - profitability, liquidity, leverage, efficiency, coverage and cash-flow ratios - and of how to interpret them in the context of the business and its industry. Industry research: building a clear picture of an industry's structure, growth and competitive dynamics, and relating a company's numbers to it. Financial modelling in Excel: three-statement spreads, cash-flow and debt-service coverage projections. Working knowledge of Ind AS, including lease accounting and its effect on leverage metrics. Assessment of financial health, earnings quality and credit risk. Familiarity with statutory and exchange disclosures (MCA, SEBI/BSE/NSE) and commercial financial databases. Production of client-ready reports and presentations in Word and PowerPoint to a defined house style. 
 Professional Skills:- Strong logical reasoning and structured problem solving - essential. Rigour with data: gaps are disclosed, never silently estimated. Neutral, factual writing with specifics in place of adjectives. Attention to detail at the level of audit opinion wording and footnote disclosures. Self-directed remote working: several assignments in parallel, disciplined version control, deadlines met without supervision. Clear, concise written communication; comfortable working from short briefs with rapid iteration. 
 Working Arrangement:- Fully remote within India; no office attendance required. Core hours 10:00-18:00 IST, with flexibility for occasional client calls outside these hours. Written-first collaboration with disciplined version control on all deliverables. Access to the firm's data subscriptions, templates and analytical models. Direct working relationship with the founder, including review of each deliverable before client release. 
 What We Offer:- A senior individual-contributor role with direct influence on methodology and the firm's research products. Breadth of work: listed and unlisted companies across industries, credit and equity perspectives, and alternative data alongside audited financials. Full-time, fully remote employment. 

 How to Apply 
 Send the following to partner@digially.ai: 
 Curriculum vitae. Two authored writing samples - company analyses or research reports, redacted as necessary. A short note (under 300 words) on one Indian company whose reported financials you would question, and why. 
 Selection Process 
 Expected duration: 2-3 weeks end to end Screening Call (30 minutes) Take-home Case (3-4 hours): Analysis of a company from its audited financials and filings - ratio analysis, a cash flow statement built from the balance sheet and P&L, and a short written view on the business. Technical Interview: Interview with the founder covering the case and the writing samples. Reference Checks and Offer 
 DigiAlly is an equal opportunity employer. Selection is based solely on the quality of a candidate's analysis and writing.
